q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Cashier – One who receives and pays out money in a bank or shop
Fugitive – One who has escaped from captivity or is running away from justice
Maestro – One who checks and verifies accounts
Accomplice – One who helps another in committing a crime
exp: 'Maestro' means 'A distinguished conductor or musician' (संगीत-आचार्य), not 'One who checks and verifies accounts' (that is 'auditor'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who is held captive as security for the fulfilment of a demand
exp: 'One who is held captive as security for the fulfilment of a demand' is called 'hostage' (Hindi: बंधक). Other options: vegan (पूर्ण शाकाहारी (वीगन)); broker (दलाल); landlord (मकान-मालिक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to the sea
exp: 'Relating to the sea' is called 'marine' (Hindi: समुद्री). Other options: contagious (संक्रामक (छूत का)); immortal (अमर); oral (मौखिक).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: FRAGILE
exp: FRAGILE (Hindi: भंगुर, नाज़ुक) means: Easily broken. The other options are the meanings of maternal, obsolete, immortal respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A doctor who specialises in heart diseases
exp: 'A doctor who specialises in heart diseases' is called 'cardiologist' (Hindi: हृदय-रोग विशेषज्ञ). Other options: sadist (परपीड़क); widower (विधुर); narcissist (आत्ममुग्ध).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: BELLIGERENT
opts: One who is engaged in a war
That cannot be wounded or harmed
That cannot be crossed or travelled over
exp: BELLIGERENT (Hindi: युद्धरत) means: One who is engaged in a war. The other options are the meanings of omniscient, invulnerable, impassable respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who helps another in committing a crime
exp: 'One who helps another in committing a crime' is called 'accomplice' (Hindi: अपराध में सहभागी). Other options: goldsmith (सुनार); philanthropist (परोपकारी, लोकहितैषी); gourmet (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का पारखी).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who has no religious faith or follows a different religion
exp: 'One who has no religious faith or follows a different religion' is called 'infidel' (Hindi: काफ़िर, अविश्वासी). Other options: cardiologist (हृदय-रोग विशेषज्ञ); charlatan (ढोंगी, नीम-हकीम); dermatologist (त्वचा-रोग विशेषज्ञ).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Armoury – A place where weapons are kept
Burrow – A hole dug by a rabbit or a fox
Mortuary – A place where ships are built or repaired
Menagerie – A collection of wild animals kept for exhibition
exp: 'Mortuary' means 'A place where dead bodies are kept for a short time' (शवगृह), not 'A place where ships are built or repaired' (that is 'dockyard'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: That can be done easily
exp: 'That can be done easily' is called 'feasible' (Hindi: व्यवहार्य, संभव). Other options: mortal (नश्वर); portable (सुवाह्य, ले जाने योग्य); solar (सौर).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: That cannot be cured
exp: 'That cannot be cured' is called 'incurable' (Hindi: असाध्य). Other options: legible (पठनीय, सुपाठ्य); feline (बिल्ली-संबंधी); indelible (अमिट).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: CLICHÉ
opts: A list of difficult words with their meanings at the end of a book
Obtaining money by force or threats
The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property
An idea or phrase that has been overused
exp: CLICHÉ (Hindi: घिसा-पिटा कथन) means: An idea or phrase that has been overused. The other options are the meanings of glossary, arson, extortion respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A place where government or historical records are kept
exp: 'A place where government or historical records are kept' is called 'archives' (Hindi: अभिलेखागार). Other options: den (माँद); nursery (पौधशाला); mint (टकसाल).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Of unknown or unnamed authorship
exp: 'Of unknown or unnamed authorship' is called 'anonymous' (Hindi: अज्ञात, अनाम). Other options: marine (समुद्री); unanimous (सर्वसम्मत); oral (मौखिक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: An idea or phrase that has been overused
exp: 'An idea or phrase that has been overused' is called 'cliché' (Hindi: घिसा-पिटा कथन). Other options: slander (मौखिक मानहानि); endemic (स्थानिक रोग); forgery (जालसाज़ी).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Souvenir – An introductory section of a play or book
Prologue – A brief summary of a book or play
Synopsis – A thing kept as a reminder of a person, place or event
exp: Bouquet (गुलदस्ता) means 'A bunch of flowers'. Correct meanings of the others: prologue = An introductory section of a play or book; synopsis = A brief summary of a book or play; souvenir = A thing kept as a reminder of a person, place or event.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Agoraphobia – A mania for power or grandeur
Acrophobia – Fear of open or public places
exp: Pyrophobia (अग्नि-भय) means 'Fear of fire'. Correct meanings of the others: agoraphobia = Fear of open or public places; megalomania = A mania for power or grandeur; acrophobia = Fear of heights.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Gourmet – One who loves mankind and works for its welfare
Sculptor – A connoisseur of good food and drink
Mercenary – A soldier who fights for any country for money
Philanthropist – One who carves figures in stone or wood
exp: Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक) means 'A soldier who fights for any country for money'. Correct meanings of the others: gourmet = A connoisseur of good food and drink; philanthropist = One who loves mankind and works for its welfare; sculptor = One who carves figures in stone or wood.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: LEONINE
exp: LEONINE (Hindi: सिंह-संबंधी) means: Relating to lions. The other options are the meanings of sartorial, extempore, arboreal respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: AFFIDAVIT
opts: A false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
A written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence in court
The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property
Special words used by a particular profession and hard for others to understand
exp: AFFIDAVIT (Hindi: शपथ-पत्र, हलफ़नामा) means: A written statement confirmed by oath for use as evidence in court. The other options are the meanings of slander, arson, jargon respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of the nervous system
exp: 'The study of the nervous system' is called 'neurology' (Hindi: तंत्रिका-विज्ञान). Other options: zoology (प्राणिशास्त्र); horticulture (बागवानी, उद्यान-विज्ञान); genealogy (वंशावली-विज्ञान).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A place from where stars and planets are observed
exp: 'A place from where stars and planets are observed' is called 'observatory' (Hindi: वेधशाला). Other options: library (पुस्तकालय); nursery (पौधशाला); cemetery (क़ब्रिस्तान).

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Arboreal; (B) Soliloquy; (C) Hedonist; (D) Alliteration
List-II: (1) One who believes that pleasure is the chief good in life; (2) Living in trees; (3) Repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words; (4) Speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play
exp: Correct matching: Arboreal = Living in trees; Soliloquy = Speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, especially in a play; Hedonist = One who believes that pleasure is the chief good in life; Alliteration = Repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words. Hence A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ALLEGORY
opts: Violation or misuse of something regarded as sacred
A speech or writing in praise of a person, especially one who has died
A story in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas
exp: ALLEGORY (Hindi: रूपक-कथा) means: A story in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas. The other options are the meanings of epitaph, sacrilege, eulogy respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Violation or misuse of something regarded as sacred
exp: 'Violation or misuse of something regarded as sacred' is called 'sacrilege' (Hindi: अपवित्रीकरण). Other options: anagram (वर्णविपर्यय शब्द); allegory (रूपक-कथा); euphemism (प्रियोक्ति, मृदूक्ति).

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Glutton – One who eats too much
Paediatrician – One who copies another's writing and passes it off as his own
Theist – One who believes in the existence of God
Centenarian – One who is a hundred years old or more
exp: 'Paediatrician' means 'A doctor who specialises in children's diseases' (बाल-रोग विशेषज्ञ), not 'One who copies another's writing and passes it off as his own' (that is 'plagiarist'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: Relating to the eyes
exp: 'Relating to the eyes' is called 'ocular' (Hindi: नेत्र-संबंधी). Other options: fastidious (नकचढ़ा, जिसे प्रसन्न करना कठिन हो); diurnal (दिनचर); irrevocable (अपरिवर्तनीय, अटल).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: INEVITABLE
opts: Relating to a town or city
exp: INEVITABLE (Hindi: अपरिहार्य, अवश्यंभावी) means: That cannot be avoided. The other options are the meanings of manual, portable, urban respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Oasis – A place where aircraft are kept
Kennel – A fertile spot in a desert where water is found
exp: Orphanage (अनाथालय) means 'A home for orphans'. Correct meanings of the others: oasis = A fertile spot in a desert where water is found; hangar = A place where aircraft are kept; kennel = A shelter for dogs.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who regards the whole world as his country
exp: 'One who regards the whole world as his country' is called 'cosmopolitan' (Hindi: विश्वनागरिक). Other options: mediator (मध्यस्थ); hermit (संन्यासी, वैरागी); proprietor (स्वामी, मालिक).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A period of fourteen days
exp: 'A period of fourteen days' is called 'fortnight' (Hindi: पखवाड़ा). Other options: libel (अपलेख, मानहानि-लेख); bribery (रिश्वतख़ोरी); smuggling (तस्करी).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: PLACEBO
opts: A published false statement damaging to a person's reputation
The point in the sky directly overhead
A collection of poems or other writings by various authors
A harmless substance given as medicine for psychological effect
exp: PLACEBO (Hindi: प्लेसीबो (भ्रामक औषधि)) means: A harmless substance given as medicine for psychological effect. The other options are the meanings of zenith, anthology, libel respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of birds
exp: 'The study of birds' is called 'ornithology' (Hindi: पक्षीविज्ञान). Other options: sericulture (रेशम-कीट पालन); osteology (अस्थि-विज्ञान); pisciculture (मत्स्य-पालन).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: QUACK
opts: One who pretends to have medical skill
One who believes that nothing can be known about the existence of God
One who sneers at the aims and beliefs of others and believes people act only from self-interest
One who abstains from marriage and sexual relations
exp: QUACK (Hindi: नीम-हकीम, झोलाछाप डॉक्टर) means: One who pretends to have medical skill. The other options are the meanings of celibate, agnostic, cynic respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: PATRIOT
opts: One who loves his country and is ready to defend it
The leading character in a play or story
One who makes things out of wood
exp: PATRIOT (Hindi: देशभक्त) means: One who loves his country and is ready to defend it. The other options are the meanings of protagonist, architect, carpenter respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A final demand with a threat of action if it is rejected
exp: 'A final demand with a threat of action if it is rejected' is called 'ultimatum' (Hindi: अंतिम चेतावनी). Other options: constellation (तारामंडल); fable (नीतिकथा); golden jubilee (स्वर्ण जयंती).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: DIAMOND JUBILEE
opts: A list of difficult words with their meanings at the end of a book
A brief summary of a book or play
An open rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors
exp: DIAMOND JUBILEE (Hindi: हीरक जयंती) means: The sixtieth anniversary. The other options are the meanings of mutiny, synopsis, glossary respectively.

q:
Match the words in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Glossary; (B) Auditory; (C) Slander; (D) Bureaucracy
List-II: (1) A list of difficult words with their meanings at the end of a book; (2) Government by officials; (3) Relating to the sense of hearing; (4) A false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation
exp: Correct matching: Glossary = A list of difficult words with their meanings at the end of a book; Auditory = Relating to the sense of hearing; Slander = A false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation; Bureaucracy = Government by officials. Hence A-1, B-3, C-4, D-2.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: BENEFICIARY
opts: One who is new to a trade or occupation
One who makes things out of gold
One who receives benefit from a will or insurance
exp: BENEFICIARY (Hindi: लाभार्थी) means: One who receives benefit from a will or insurance. The other options are the meanings of goldsmith, proprietor, novice respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Claustrophobia – Fear of closed or narrow spaces
exp: 'Megalomania' means 'A mania for power or grandeur' (महत्ता-सनक, सत्ता का उन्माद), not 'Fear of being alone' (that is 'monophobia'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The study of the eye and its diseases
exp: 'The study of the eye and its diseases' is called 'ophthalmology' (Hindi: नेत्र-विज्ञान). Other options: cartography (मानचित्र-कला); philology (भाषाविज्ञान (भाषाशास्त्र)); calligraphy (सुलेख).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who can speak two languages fluently
exp: 'One who can speak two languages fluently' is called 'bilingual' (Hindi: द्विभाषी). Other options: beneficiary (लाभार्थी); mediator (मध्यस्थ); novice (नौसिखिया).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: INFANTRY
opts: The decision of a jury or court on a case
The line at which the earth and sky appear to meet
A system or period of government
exp: INFANTRY (Hindi: पैदल सेना) means: Soldiers who fight on foot. The other options are the meanings of regime, verdict, horizon respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is CORRECTLY matched?
opts: Potable – That cannot be wounded or harmed
exp: Irreparable (जिसकी मरम्मत न हो सके) means 'That cannot be repaired'. Correct meanings of the others: potable = Fit to drink; invulnerable = That cannot be wounded or harmed; omniscient = One who knows everything.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: The act of killing oneself
exp: 'The act of killing oneself' is called 'suicide' (Hindi: आत्महत्या). Other options: pesticide (पीड़कनाशी); matriarchy (मातृसत्ता); oligarchy (अल्पतंत्र).

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: SOCIOLOGY
opts: The study of the earth's crust and rocks
The study of religion and God
The study of ancient remains and monuments
exp: SOCIOLOGY (Hindi: समाजशास्त्र) means: The study of human society. The other options are the meanings of theology, archaeology, geology respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: DENTAL
exp: DENTAL (Hindi: दाँत-संबंधी) means: Relating to the teeth. The other options are the meanings of annual, oral, visual respectively.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: VACCINE
opts: The life story of a person written by himself
An imitation of a writer's style for comic effect
A substance used to produce immunity against a disease
exp: VACCINE (Hindi: टीका) means: A substance used to produce immunity against a disease. The other options are the meanings of infantry, parody, autobiography respectively.

q: Which of the following word–meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Ultimatum – A final demand with a threat of action if it is rejected
Anthology – Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things
Dialect – A form of a language spoken in a particular region
Arson – The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property
exp: 'Anthology' means 'A collection of poems or other writings by various authors' (संकलन), not 'Speaking disrespectfully about God or sacred things' (that is 'blasphemy'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the expression that best explains the meaning of the word: ASTROLOGY
opts: The study of family history and lineage
The study of the influence of stars on human affairs
exp: ASTROLOGY (Hindi: ज्योतिष) means: The study of the influence of stars on human affairs. The other options are the meanings of genealogy, botany, zoology respectively.

q: Choose the one word substitute for: A young person below the age of adulthood
exp: 'A young person below the age of adulthood' is called 'juvenile' (Hindi: किशोर, अवयस्क). Other options: pedestrian (पैदल यात्री); widow (विधवा); dictator (तानाशाह).

q: Choose the one word substitute for: One who is outgoing and socially confident
exp: 'One who is outgoing and socially confident' is called 'extrovert' (Hindi: बहिर्मुखी). Other options: octogenarian (अस्सी वर्षीय); epicure (भोगी, स्वादप्रेमी); spendthrift (फ़िज़ूलख़र्च).

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a golden handshake'
opts: a task that has no hope of success
a large payment given to someone leaving a job
exp: 'a golden handshake' means 'a large payment given to someone leaving a job' (Hindi: सेवानिवृत्ति पर दी जाने वाली बड़ी राशि). The other options are the meanings of 'on the spur of the moment'; 'a baker's dozen'; 'a fool's errand' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a constant source of annoyance'
exp: 'a thorn in the flesh' means 'a constant source of annoyance' (Hindi: लगातार परेशानी का कारण). Others: 'a wolf in sheep's clothing' = a dangerous person pretending to be harmless; 'die in harness' = to die while still working; 'a Himalayan blunder' = a very big mistake.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'in a very difficult situation with no escape'
exp: 'back to the wall' means 'in a very difficult situation with no escape' (Hindi: बहुत कठिन स्थिति में). Others: 'at a loss' = unable to decide what to do; 'be all and end all' = the most important part; 'in black and white' = in writing.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Wear one's heart on one's sleeve – think carefully before acting
Lend an ear – to listen attentively
Beside the mark – to show one's feelings openly
exp: 'lend an ear' means 'to listen attentively' (ध्यान से सुनना). Correct meanings of the others: 'beside the mark' = irrelevant; 'wear one's heart on one's sleeve' = to show one's feelings openly; 'look before you leap' = think carefully before acting.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'eat one's heart out'
opts: to suffer in silence from grief or envy
exp: 'eat one's heart out' means 'to suffer in silence from grief or envy' (Hindi: मन ही मन कुढ़ना). The other options are the meanings of 'give and take'; 'all at sea'; 'come to a head' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'drive home'
exp: 'drive home' means 'to make something clearly understood' (Hindi: अच्छी तरह समझाना). The other options are the meanings of 'with a high hand'; 'see red'; 'a cut above' respectively.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Lick one's boots; (B) Rack one's brains; (C) Sink or swim; (D) A black sheep
List-II: (1) to flatter servilely; (2) to fail or succeed by one's own efforts; (3) a person who brings disgrace to the family or group; (4) to think very hard
exp: Correct matching: 'lick one's boots' = to flatter servilely; 'rack one's brains' = to think very hard; 'sink or swim' = to fail or succeed by one's own efforts; 'a black sheep' = a person who brings disgrace to the family or group. Hence A-1, B-4, C-2, D-3.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'hard and fast'
opts: to withdraw from an agreement or promise
exp: 'hard and fast' means 'strict and fixed (rule)' (Hindi: कठोर और निश्चित). The other options are the meanings of 'a cut above'; 'a red letter day'; 'back out' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'level in a race or competition'
exp: 'neck and neck' means 'level in a race or competition' (Hindi: बराबरी पर). Others: 'play to the gallery' = to try to win popular approval; 'hang fire' = to be delayed; 'keep at bay' = to keep at a distance.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'out of the wood'
opts: to find fault with a gift
exp: 'out of the wood' means 'out of danger or difficulty' (Hindi: ख़तरे से बाहर). The other options are the meanings of 'through thick and thin'; 'look a gift horse in the mouth'; 'cat and dog life' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a narrow escape'
opts: escape from danger with very little margin
to find fault with a gift
exp: 'a narrow escape' means 'escape from danger with very little margin' (Hindi: बाल-बाल बचना). The other options are the meanings of 'fly off the handle'; 'let the cat out of the bag'; 'look a gift horse in the mouth' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'throw dust in one's eyes'
opts: to try to win popular approval
exp: 'throw dust in one's eyes' means 'to deceive' (Hindi: आँखों में धूल झोंकना). The other options are the meanings of 'play to the gallery'; 'true to one's salt'; 'a wolf at the door' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'in a position of control'
exp: 'at the helm of affairs' means 'in a position of control' (Hindi: सत्ता या नियंत्रण में). Others: 'crocodile tears' = false or insincere sorrow; 'a far-fetched idea' = an idea that is unlikely to be true; 'a golden handshake' = a large payment given to someone leaving a job.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Turn a deaf ear; (B) A rule of thumb; (C) Draw in one's horns; (D) A man of straw
List-II: (1) to refuse to listen; (2) to become more cautious; to reduce spending; (3) a person of no substance or means; (4) a practical method based on experience
exp: Correct matching: 'turn a deaf ear' = to refuse to listen; 'a rule of thumb' = a practical method based on experience; 'draw in one's horns' = to become more cautious; to reduce spending; 'a man of straw' = a person of no substance or means. Hence A-1, B-4, C-2, D-3.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Flog a dead horse – to waste effort on a finished matter
Call a spade a spade – to speak plainly and frankly
Haul over the coals – very quickly
Walk on eggshells – to be very careful not to upset someone
exp: 'haul over the coals' means 'to scold severely' (कड़ी फटकार लगाना), not 'very quickly' (that is the meaning of 'in a jiffy'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'of the kind one likes'
exp: 'after one's own heart' means 'of the kind one likes' (Hindi: मनपसंद). Others: 'with open arms' = warmly, with great welcome; 'in the air' = uncertain; being rumoured; 'come to a head' = to reach a crisis.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'few and far between'
exp: 'few and far between' means 'very rare' (Hindi: बहुत कम, विरल). The other options are the meanings of 'hard and fast'; 'dead against'; 'take French leave' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a busman's holiday'
opts: at a distance, avoiding close contact
a large payment given to someone leaving a job
a holiday spent doing one's usual work
a bribe to quieten a troublesome person
exp: 'a busman's holiday' means 'a holiday spent doing one's usual work' (Hindi: छुट्टी में भी अपना ही काम करना). The other options are the meanings of 'a sop to Cerberus'; 'at arm's length'; 'a golden handshake' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'dead against'
opts: to do something never done before

Knock into shape – a matter to complain or argue about
Through thick and thin – under all circumstances
exp: 'knock into shape' means 'to make something orderly or efficient' (ठीक-ठाक करना, व्यवस्थित करना), not 'a matter to complain or argue about' (that is the meaning of 'a bone to pick'). The other pairs are correct.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Set the Thames on fire; (B) Fish in troubled waters; (C) Make a clean sweep; (D) When pigs fly
List-II: (1) to take advantage of a confused situation; (2) to remove completely; (3) to do something remarkable; (4) never
exp: Correct matching: 'set the Thames on fire' = to do something remarkable; 'fish in troubled waters' = to take advantage of a confused situation; 'make a clean sweep' = to remove completely; 'when pigs fly' = never. Hence A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'at a distance, avoiding close contact'
exp: 'at arm's length' means 'at a distance, avoiding close contact' (Hindi: दूरी बनाकर रखना). Others: 'throw down the gauntlet' = to issue a challenge; 'of no avail' = of no use; 'a turncoat' = a person who changes sides or principles.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'dance to someone's tune'
opts: a hope or plan that is very unlikely to be realised
exp: 'dance to someone's tune' means 'to obey someone without question' (Hindi: किसी के इशारों पर नाचना). The other options are the meanings of 'make one's blood boil'; 'a pie in the sky'; 'null and void' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to try to do more than one is able to'
opts: Bite off more than one can chew
exp: 'bite off more than one can chew' means 'to try to do more than one is able to' (Hindi: सामर्थ्य से अधिक काम लेना). Others: 'die in harness' = to die while still working; 'a moot point' = a debatable question; 'in the doldrums' = in low spirits; inactive.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to tease or make fun of someone'
opts: Keep the wolf from the door
exp: 'pull one's leg' means 'to tease or make fun of someone' (Hindi: मज़ाक उड़ाना, छेड़ना). Others: 'in the pink' = in very good health and spirits; 'keep the wolf from the door' = to avoid starvation; 'knock into shape' = to make something orderly or efficient.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'make hay while the sun shines'
opts: a bribe to quieten a troublesome person
to make the best use of an opportunity
a person who helps others in need unselfishly
exp: 'make hay while the sun shines' means 'to make the best use of an opportunity' (Hindi: अवसर का लाभ उठाना). The other options are the meanings of 'a sop to Cerberus'; 'all moonshine'; 'a good Samaritan' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Flesh and blood – to maintain an outward show
A pie in the sky – a hope or plan that is very unlikely to be realised
A queer fish – a strange person
Pour oil on troubled waters – to calm a quarrel
exp: 'flesh and blood' means 'human nature; one's relatives' (मानव स्वभाव, सगे-संबंधी), not 'to maintain an outward show' (that is the meaning of 'keep up appearances'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to bribe'
exp: 'grease the palm' means 'to bribe' (Hindi: रिश्वत देना). Others: 'go haywire' = to go out of control; 'at the helm of affairs' = in a position of control; 'rest on one's laurels' = to be satisfied with past success and stop trying.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'off and on'
opts: to suffer in silence from grief or envy
to face the consequences of one's actions
exp: 'off and on' means 'occasionally' (Hindi: कभी-कभी). The other options are the meanings of 'eat one's heart out'; 'face the music'; 'foot the bill' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to get no result'
opts: Take the bull by the horns
exp: 'draw a blank' means 'to get no result' (Hindi: कोई परिणाम न मिलना). Others: 'clip someone's wings' = to restrict someone's freedom; 'take the bull by the horns' = to face a difficulty boldly; 'a bed of roses' = an easy and comfortable situation.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'rule the roost'
opts: to dominate; to be in charge
to have a false sense of happiness
exp: 'rule the roost' means 'to dominate; to be in charge' (Hindi: दबदबा होना). The other options are the meanings of 'live in a fool's paradise'; 'an apple of discord'; 'spick and span' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'know which side one's bread is buttered'
opts: to know where one's advantage lies
to be satisfied with past success and stop trying
an idea that is unlikely to be true
exp: 'know which side one's bread is buttered' means 'to know where one's advantage lies' (Hindi: अपना हित पहचानना). The other options are the meanings of 'lion's share'; 'a far-fetched idea'; 'rest on one's laurels' respectively.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Fish in troubled waters; (B) Pull strings; (C) A maiden speech; (D) Rub salt into the wound
List-II: (1) to take advantage of a confused situation; (2) to make a painful situation worse; (3) to use one's influence secretly; (4) the first speech of a person in parliament or public
exp: Correct matching: 'fish in troubled waters' = to take advantage of a confused situation; 'pull strings' = to use one's influence secretly; 'a maiden speech' = the first speech of a person in parliament or public; 'rub salt into the wound' = to make a painful situation worse. Hence A-1, B-3, C-4, D-2.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Make a mountain of a molehill – to live a miserable life
Cast a slur – to bring disgrace to
Make hay while the sun shines – to make the best use of an opportunity
Dog in the manger – a person who neither uses a thing himself nor lets others use it
exp: 'make a mountain of a molehill' means 'to exaggerate a minor problem' (राई का पहाड़ बनाना), not 'to live a miserable life' (that is the meaning of 'lead a dog's life'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'keep one's head'
opts: to stop working for the day
to remain calm in a crisis
exp: 'keep one's head' means 'to remain calm in a crisis' (Hindi: संकट में शांत रहना). The other options are the meanings of 'call it a day'; 'put one's foot in it'; 'a man of parts' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Pick holes in – to find fault with
Salt of the earth – a person of great worth
In the teeth of – in spite of strong opposition
exp: 'on the cards' means 'likely to happen' (संभावित), not 'thoroughly, completely' (that is the meaning of 'root and branch'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'bite off more than one can chew'
opts: to try to do more than one is able to
exp: 'bite off more than one can chew' means 'to try to do more than one is able to' (Hindi: सामर्थ्य से अधिक काम लेना). The other options are the meanings of 'a thorn in the flesh'; 'off the cuff'; 'run amuck' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Play second fiddle – to take a subordinate role
By hook or by crook – to have a false sense of happiness
Make amends – to compensate for a wrong
Walk on eggshells – to be very careful not to upset someone
exp: 'by hook or by crook' means 'by any means, fair or foul' (किसी भी तरह, येन-केन-प्रकारेण), not 'to have a false sense of happiness' (that is the meaning of 'live in a fool's paradise'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'show a clean pair of heels'
opts: to run away quickly and escape
to say exactly the right thing
exp: 'show a clean pair of heels' means 'to run away quickly and escape' (Hindi: भाग जाना). The other options are the meanings of 'pour oil on troubled waters'; 'keep up appearances'; 'hit the nail on the head' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make a poor impression'
opts: Give a piece of one's mind
exp: 'cut a sorry figure' means 'to make a poor impression' (Hindi: बुरी छाप छोड़ना, हास्यास्पद दिखना). Others: 'eat one's heart out' = to suffer in silence from grief or envy; 'give a piece of one's mind' = to scold frankly; 'carry the day' = to win.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) In the pink; (B) A narrow escape; (C) Fill the bill; (D) Move heaven and earth
List-II: (1) to try every possible means to achieve something; (2) escape from danger with very little margin; (3) to be suitable for a purpose; (4) in very good health and spirits
exp: Correct matching: 'in the pink' = in very good health and spirits; 'a narrow escape' = escape from danger with very little margin; 'fill the bill' = to be suitable for a purpose; 'move heaven and earth' = to try every possible means to achieve something. Hence A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'lick one's boots'
opts: to behave in an uncontrolled way
a costly possession that is useless or troublesome
exp: 'lick one's boots' means 'to flatter servilely' (Hindi: चापलूसी करना). The other options are the meanings of 'born with a silver spoon in one's mouth'; 'a white elephant'; 'run riot' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'walk on eggshells'
opts: to make money dishonestly for oneself
a lot of fuss about a small matter
to be very careful not to upset someone
exp: 'walk on eggshells' means 'to be very careful not to upset someone' (Hindi: बहुत सावधानी बरतना). The other options are the meanings of 'feather one's nest'; 'make a beeline for'; 'a storm in a teacup' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'with just enough to survive'
exp: 'from hand to mouth' means 'with just enough to survive' (Hindi: मुश्किल से गुज़ारा करना). Others: 'set one's heart on' = to desire greatly; 'in the good books' = in favour; 'look down upon' = to regard with contempt.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'clip someone's wings'
opts: to admit that one was wrong
to remain neutral; to be undecided
exp: 'clip someone's wings' means 'to restrict someone's freedom' (Hindi: पर कतरना, स्वतंत्रता सीमित करना). The other options are the meanings of 'turn a deaf ear'; 'eat crow'; 'sit on the fence' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'spick and span'
opts: a person unsuited to his job
a dangerous person pretending to be harmless
exp: 'spick and span' means 'neat and clean' (Hindi: साफ़-सुथरा). The other options are the meanings of 'as cool as a cucumber'; 'a wolf in sheep's clothing'; 'square peg in a round hole' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'skate on thin ice'
opts: to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often neglecting quality
to be in a risky situation
exp: 'skate on thin ice' means 'to be in a risky situation' (Hindi: जोखिम भरी स्थिति में होना). The other options are the meanings of 'cut corners'; 'in vain'; 'as bold as brass' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: At random – a decisive test of value or quality
An acid test – level in a race or competition
Neck and neck – without any plan or purpose
In the pink – in very good health and spirits
exp: 'in the pink' means 'in very good health and spirits' (पूर्णतः स्वस्थ). Correct meanings of the others: 'at random' = without any plan or purpose; 'an acid test' = a decisive test of value or quality; 'neck and neck' = level in a race or competition.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'play second fiddle'
opts: to make peace and end a quarrel
an idea that is unlikely to be true
exp: 'play second fiddle' means 'to take a subordinate role' (Hindi: अधीनस्थ भूमिका निभाना). The other options are the meanings of 'a far-fetched idea'; 'beggar description'; 'bury the hatchet' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'the final problem that makes a situation unbearable'
exp: 'the last straw' means 'the final problem that makes a situation unbearable' (Hindi: अंतिम असहनीय बात). Others: 'hand in glove' = very intimate, working closely together (often in wrongdoing); 'come off with flying colours' = to succeed brilliantly; 'bag and baggage' = with all one's belongings.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to break a promise'
exp: 'go back on one's word' means 'to break a promise' (Hindi: वचन से मुकर जाना). Others: 'wind up' = to bring to an end; 'from hand to mouth' = with just enough to survive; 'eat one's words' = to take back what one has said.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'run riot'
opts: to behave in an uncontrolled way
exp: 'run riot' means 'to behave in an uncontrolled way' (Hindi: उपद्रव मचाना). The other options are the meanings of 'flesh and blood'; 'within an ace of'; 'keep up appearances' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Run amuck – to behave wildly and violently
Die in harness – to die while still working
Cry over spilt milk – completely extinct or out of date
A golden handshake – a large payment given to someone leaving a job
exp: 'cry over spilt milk' means 'to regret something that cannot be undone' (बीती बात पर पछताना), not 'completely extinct or out of date' (that is the meaning of 'as dead as a dodo'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a feather in one's cap'
opts: an achievement to be proud of
a large payment given to someone leaving a job
completely extinct or out of date
exp: 'a feather in one's cap' means 'an achievement to be proud of' (Hindi: गौरव की बात, उपलब्धि). The other options are the meanings of 'die in harness'; 'as dead as a dodo'; 'a golden handshake' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Take to one's heels – to run away
Out of sorts – slightly unwell or upset
A rule of thumb – a practical method based on experience
Cool one's heels – irregularly; not continuously
exp: 'cool one's heels' means 'to be kept waiting' (प्रतीक्षा करते रहना), not 'irregularly; not continuously' (that is the meaning of 'by fits and starts'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: A dog's life – a miserable existence
Dog in the manger – empty talk, nonsense
All moonshine – to be impossible to describe
Beggar description – a person who neither uses a thing himself nor lets others use it
exp: 'a dog's life' means 'a miserable existence' (दयनीय जीवन). Correct meanings of the others: 'all moonshine' = empty talk, nonsense; 'beggar description' = to be impossible to describe; 'dog in the manger' = a person who neither uses a thing himself nor lets others use it.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Pull one's leg – to make a bad situation worse
Burn the midnight oil – to work or study late into the night
Over the moon – to tease or make fun of someone
Add fuel to the fire – extremely happy
exp: 'burn the midnight oil' means 'to work or study late into the night' (देर रात तक पढ़ना/काम करना). Correct meanings of the others: 'pull one's leg' = to tease or make fun of someone; 'add fuel to the fire' = to make a bad situation worse; 'over the moon' = extremely happy.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a state of hostility without actual fighting'
exp: 'a cold war' means 'a state of hostility without actual fighting' (Hindi: शीत युद्ध, अप्रत्यक्ष शत्रुता). Others: 'after one's own heart' = of the kind one likes; 'bring to book' = to punish or call to account; 'vote with one's feet' = to show disapproval by leaving.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Chew the cud – one who criticises without practical experience
Cut the Gordian knot – to reflect or think deeply
At daggers drawn – bitterly hostile to each other
An armchair critic – to solve a difficult problem by bold action
exp: 'at daggers drawn' means 'bitterly hostile to each other' (कट्टर शत्रुता में). Correct meanings of the others: 'an armchair critic' = one who criticises without practical experience; 'cut the Gordian knot' = to solve a difficult problem by bold action; 'chew the cud' = to reflect or think deeply.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'strict and harsh control'
exp: 'an iron hand' means 'strict and harsh control' (Hindi: कठोर नियंत्रण). Others: 'on the cards' = likely to happen; 'throw dust in one's eyes' = to deceive; 'a tall order' = a very difficult demand.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make the best use of an opportunity'
opts: Make hay while the sun shines
On the spur of the moment
exp: 'make hay while the sun shines' means 'to make the best use of an opportunity' (Hindi: अवसर का लाभ उठाना). Others: 'from the horse's mouth' = directly from the original source; 'on the spur of the moment' = suddenly, without planning; 'mind one's p's and q's' = to be careful about one's behaviour.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'make one's blood boil'
opts: to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often neglecting quality
to remain neutral; to be undecided
exp: 'make one's blood boil' means 'to make someone very angry' (Hindi: ख़ून खौलना). The other options are the meanings of 'cut corners'; 'sit on the fence'; 'as the crow flies' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'salt of the earth'
opts: a decisive test of value or quality
exp: 'salt of the earth' means 'a person of great worth' (Hindi: अत्यंत भला व्यक्ति). The other options are the meanings of 'an acid test'; 'in a fix'; 'keep one's fingers crossed' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'when pigs fly'
exp: 'when pigs fly' means 'never' (Hindi: कभी नहीं). The other options are the meanings of 'take with a pinch of salt'; 'within an ace of'; 'kick the bucket' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'something supposed to be secret but known to all'
exp: 'an open secret' means 'something supposed to be secret but known to all' (Hindi: जगज़ाहिर रहस्य). Others: 'go to the wall' = to be ruined; to fail in business; 'keep one's head' = to remain calm in a crisis; 'die hard' = to change or disappear very slowly.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to scold frankly'
opts: Give a piece of one's mind
exp: 'give a piece of one's mind' means 'to scold frankly' (Hindi: खरी-खोटी सुनाना). Others: 'be all and end all' = the most important part; 'look down upon' = to regard with contempt; 'save one's skin' = to escape from danger or punishment.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'to the backbone'
opts: a bribe to quieten a troublesome person
a person used as a tool by another
exp: 'to the backbone' means 'thoroughly; completely' (Hindi: पूर्णतः, पक्का). The other options are the meanings of 'a dog's chance'; 'a cat's paw'; 'a sop to Cerberus' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'faced with two equally dangerous choices'
exp: 'between Scylla and Charybdis' means 'faced with two equally dangerous choices' (Hindi: इधर कुआँ उधर खाई). Others: 'at the eleventh hour' = at the last possible moment; 'by hook or by crook' = by any means, fair or foul; 'at one's wit's end' = completely puzzled and not knowing what to do.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'wind up'
opts: to face all kinds of risks and dangers
exp: 'wind up' means 'to bring to an end' (Hindi: समाप्त करना). The other options are the meanings of 'in hot water'; 'foot the bill'; 'go through fire and water' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'cry over spilt milk'
opts: to regret something that cannot be undone
something that turns out to be disappointing
exp: 'cry over spilt milk' means 'to regret something that cannot be undone' (Hindi: बीती बात पर पछताना). The other options are the meanings of 'at daggers drawn'; 'a pretty kettle of fish'; 'a damp squib' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to punish or call to account'
exp: 'bring to book' means 'to punish or call to account' (Hindi: दंडित करना, जवाब तलब करना). Others: 'put two and two together' = to draw a conclusion from facts; 'vote with one's feet' = to show disapproval by leaving; 'at a loss' = unable to decide what to do.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to do something thoroughly'
exp: 'go the whole hog' means 'to do something thoroughly' (Hindi: पूरी तरह से करना). Others: 'mince matters' = to speak evasively to avoid offending; 'nip in the bud' = to stop something at an early stage; 'between Scylla and Charybdis' = faced with two equally dangerous choices.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to become discouraged'
exp: 'lose heart' means 'to become discouraged' (Hindi: हिम्मत हारना). Others: 'get wind of' = to hear about something secretly; 'look down upon' = to regard with contempt; 'break the news' = to reveal unpleasant news gently.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'never'
opts: On the horns of a dilemma
exp: 'when pigs fly' means 'never' (Hindi: कभी नहीं). Others: 'an olive branch' = an offer of peace; 'lose one's temper' = to become angry; 'on the horns of a dilemma' = in a situation requiring a choice between two unpleasant alternatives.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'the largest part'
opts: Know which side one's bread is buttered
exp: 'lion's share' means 'the largest part' (Hindi: सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा). Others: 'between Scylla and Charybdis' = faced with two equally dangerous choices; 'let bygones be bygones' = to forget past quarrels; 'know which side one's bread is buttered' = to know where one's advantage lies.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'fill the bill'
opts: to treat someone with deliberate coldness
to be suitable for a purpose
exp: 'fill the bill' means 'to be suitable for a purpose' (Hindi: आवश्यकता पूरी करना). The other options are the meanings of 'fly in the face of'; 'end in smoke'; 'give the cold shoulder' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Weal and woe – a general view from above
A blessing in disguise – prosperity and adversity
A stone's throw – a very short distance
A bird's eye view – something good that at first seemed bad
exp: 'a stone's throw' means 'a very short distance' (बहुत थोड़ी दूरी). Correct meanings of the others: 'a bird's eye view' = a general view from above; 'a blessing in disguise' = something good that at first seemed bad; 'weal and woe' = prosperity and adversity.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'make a clean breast of'
opts: to work or study late into the night
a sudden success that is not repeated
exp: 'make a clean breast of' means 'to confess fully' (Hindi: सब कुछ सच-सच बता देना). The other options are the meanings of 'burn one's fingers'; 'burn the midnight oil'; 'a flash in the pan' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'keep at bay'
opts: to give credit even to a bad person
exp: 'keep at bay' means 'to keep at a distance' (Hindi: दूर रखना). The other options are the meanings of 'give the devil his due'; 'let the grass grow under one's feet'; 'bread and butter' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to be careful about one's behaviour'
exp: 'mind one's p's and q's' means 'to be careful about one's behaviour' (Hindi: अपने व्यवहार में सावधान रहना). Others: 'bear the brunt' = to bear the main burden or impact; 'cast a slur' = to bring disgrace to; 'beggar description' = to be impossible to describe.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to attract one's attention'
exp: 'catch one's eye' means 'to attract one's attention' (Hindi: ध्यान आकर्षित करना). Others: 'bring to book' = to punish or call to account; 'in the good books' = in favour; 'black and blue' = badly bruised.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: An olive branch – an offer of peace
Born with a silver spoon in one's mouth – a former lover
Take with a pinch of salt – born in a rich family
An old flame – to accept with some doubt
exp: 'an olive branch' means 'an offer of peace' (शांति का प्रस्ताव). Correct meanings of the others: 'take with a pinch of salt' = to accept with some doubt; 'born with a silver spoon in one's mouth' = born in a rich family; 'an old flame' = a former lover.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Run amuck – no chance at all
In a jiffy – to behave wildly and violently
A pretty kettle of fish – an awkward or difficult situation
exp: 'a pretty kettle of fish' means 'an awkward or difficult situation' (गड़बड़झाला, कठिन स्थिति). Correct meanings of the others: 'in a jiffy' = very quickly; 'run amuck' = to behave wildly and violently; 'a dog's chance' = no chance at all.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'lion's share'
opts: a bribe to quieten a troublesome person
exp: 'lion's share' means 'the largest part' (Hindi: सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा). The other options are the meanings of 'play second fiddle'; 'leave in the lurch'; 'a sop to Cerberus' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to restrict someone's freedom'
exp: 'clip someone's wings' means 'to restrict someone's freedom' (Hindi: पर कतरना, स्वतंत्रता सीमित करना). Others: 'turn the tables' = to reverse a situation to one's advantage; 'turn a deaf ear' = to refuse to listen; 'skate on thin ice' = to be in a risky situation.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to dominate; to be in charge'
exp: 'rule the roost' means 'to dominate; to be in charge' (Hindi: दबदबा होना). Others: 'a damp squib' = something that turns out to be disappointing; 'a golden handshake' = a large payment given to someone leaving a job; 'a skeleton in the cupboard' = a shameful secret.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Bite off more than one can chew – to try to do more than one is able to
A feather in one's cap – an achievement to be proud of
A turncoat – a person who changes sides or principles
Off the cuff – a plain child who grows into a beautiful adult
exp: 'off the cuff' means 'without preparation' (बिना तैयारी के), not 'a plain child who grows into a beautiful adult' (that is the meaning of 'an ugly duckling'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'at large'
exp: 'at large' means 'free and not captured' (Hindi: फ़रार, खुला घूमना). The other options are the meanings of 'get away with'; 'a shot in the dark'; 'fair and square' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a very small amount compared with what is needed'
exp: 'a drop in the ocean' means 'a very small amount compared with what is needed' (Hindi: ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा). Others: 'take to task' = to rebuke; 'add fuel to the fire' = to make a bad situation worse; 'at a premium' = in great demand; scarce.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to hear about something secretly'
exp: 'get wind of' means 'to hear about something secretly' (Hindi: भनक लगना). Others: 'be all and end all' = the most important part; 'save one's skin' = to escape from danger or punishment; 'see the light' = to understand something at last.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'in a difficult situation'
opts: Let the grass grow under one's feet
exp: 'in a fix' means 'in a difficult situation' (Hindi: मुश्किल में). Others: 'neck and neck' = level in a race or competition; 'let the grass grow under one's feet' = to delay or waste time; 'add fuel to the fire' = to make a bad situation worse.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make a painful situation worse'
exp: 'rub salt into the wound' means 'to make a painful situation worse' (Hindi: जले पर नमक छिड़कना). Others: 'when pigs fly' = never; 'null and void' = invalid; having no legal force; 'a nest egg' = money saved for the future.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: A bed of roses – think carefully before acting
Look before you leap – to refuse to listen
Pay lip service – to support in words but not in deeds
Turn a deaf ear – an easy and comfortable situation
exp: 'pay lip service' means 'to support in words but not in deeds' (केवल मौखिक समर्थन देना). Correct meanings of the others: 'turn a deaf ear' = to refuse to listen; 'a bed of roses' = an easy and comfortable situation; 'look before you leap' = think carefully before acting.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: At a premium – in great demand; scarce
Blow hot and cold – to keep changing one's opinion
In a tight corner – in a difficult situation with little room to escape
Kick up a row – to obtain or get hold of
exp: 'kick up a row' means 'to create a disturbance' (हंगामा खड़ा करना), not 'to obtain or get hold of' (that is the meaning of 'lay one's hands on'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to be very careful not to upset someone'
opts: At the end of one's tether
exp: 'walk on eggshells' means 'to be very careful not to upset someone' (Hindi: बहुत सावधानी बरतना). Others: 'donkey's years' = a very long time; 'mince matters' = to speak evasively to avoid offending; 'at the end of one's tether' = having no patience or energy left.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'pour oil on troubled waters'
opts: to be dismissed from a job
to support in words but not in deeds
exp: 'pour oil on troubled waters' means 'to calm a quarrel' (Hindi: झगड़ा शांत करना). The other options are the meanings of 'a cock and bull story'; 'pay lip service'; 'get the sack' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'put a spoke in one's wheel'
opts: to obtain or get hold of
exp: 'put a spoke in one's wheel' means 'to obstruct someone's plans' (Hindi: काम में अड़ंगा डालना). The other options are the meanings of 'lay one's hands on'; 'make a clean breast of'; 'in the same boat' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make a bad situation worse'
exp: 'add fuel to the fire' means 'to make a bad situation worse' (Hindi: आग में घी डालना). Others: 'in a tight corner' = in a difficult situation with little room to escape; 'rise to the occasion' = to deal successfully with a difficult situation; 'an arm and a leg' = a very high price.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'break new ground'
opts: to do something never done before
to be a common trait in a family
to start a conversation in a formal or awkward situation
exp: 'break new ground' means 'to do something never done before' (Hindi: नई शुरुआत करना, नया काम करना). The other options are the meanings of 'break the ice'; 'come to a head'; 'run in the family' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a dead end'
opts: a situation from which no progress is possible
exp: 'a dead end' means 'a situation from which no progress is possible' (Hindi: गतिरोध). The other options are the meanings of 'look down upon'; 'break the news'; 'at large' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'in strong disagreement'
opts: On the spur of the moment
exp: 'at loggerheads' means 'in strong disagreement' (Hindi: घोर मतभेद में). Others: 'on the spur of the moment' = suddenly, without planning; 'an armchair critic' = one who criticises without practical experience; 'a fly in the ointment' = a small flaw that spoils something.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a fish out of water'
opts: to face the consequences of one's actions
a person in an unfamiliar and uncomfortable situation
exp: 'a fish out of water' means 'a person in an unfamiliar and uncomfortable situation' (Hindi: असहज स्थिति में व्यक्ति). The other options are the meanings of 'hold water'; 'a man of parts'; 'face the music' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a small flaw that spoils something'
exp: 'a fly in the ointment' means 'a small flaw that spoils something' (Hindi: रंग में भंग, छोटी कमी). Others: 'a skeleton in the cupboard' = a shameful secret; 'rest on one's laurels' = to be satisfied with past success and stop trying; 'to the backbone' = thoroughly; completely.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'without any plan or purpose'
exp: 'at random' means 'without any plan or purpose' (Hindi: बेतरतीब, बिना सोचे). Others: 'rain cats and dogs' = to rain very heavily; 'wash one's hands of' = to refuse to have anything more to do with; 'true to one's salt' = loyal to one's master.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to gain an advantage over someone by acting first'
exp: 'steal a march on' means 'to gain an advantage over someone by acting first' (Hindi: किसी से पहले कार्य कर बढ़त पाना). Others: 'beat about the bush' = to avoid coming to the point; 'rain cats and dogs' = to rain very heavily; 'jump the gun' = to act too soon.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to try to win popular approval'
exp: 'play to the gallery' means 'to try to win popular approval' (Hindi: सस्ती लोकप्रियता पाने का प्रयास). Others: 'in the same boat' = in the same difficult situation; 'red tape' = excessive bureaucratic formality; 'in the nick of time' = just in time.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to apologise humbly; to accept humiliation'
opts: Take with a pinch of salt
exp: 'eat humble pie' means 'to apologise humbly; to accept humiliation' (Hindi: अपमान सहकर माफ़ी माँगना). Others: 'take with a pinch of salt' = to accept with some doubt; 'on the dot' = exactly on time; 'an ivory tower' = a state of isolation from the practical realities of life.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to waste effort on a finished matter'
opts: At the end of one's tether
exp: 'flog a dead horse' means 'to waste effort on a finished matter' (Hindi: मरे हुए को मारना, व्यर्थ प्रयास). Others: 'grease the palm' = to bribe; 'a pretty kettle of fish' = an awkward or difficult situation; 'at the end of one's tether' = having no patience or energy left.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'without success'
exp: 'in vain' means 'without success' (Hindi: व्यर्थ). Others: 'brush aside' = to dismiss as unimportant; 'a lame excuse' = an unconvincing excuse; 'draw in one's horns' = to become more cautious; to reduce spending.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to take back what one has said'
exp: 'eat one's words' means 'to take back what one has said' (Hindi: अपनी बात वापस लेना). Others: 'a song and dance' = a fuss; 'a cold war' = a state of hostility without actual fighting; 'at large' = free and not captured.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Below the belt – unfair, against the rules
True to one's salt – in a difficult situation
Kill two birds with one stone – to achieve two aims with a single action
Burn the midnight oil – to work or study late into the night
exp: 'true to one's salt' means 'loyal to one's master' (नमकहलाल, वफ़ादार), not 'in a difficult situation' (that is the meaning of 'in a fix'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Put a spoke in one's wheel – to obstruct someone's plans
Wash one's hands of – to refuse to have anything more to do with
A man of letters – to act too soon
exp: 'a man of letters' means 'a scholar or literary person' (विद्वान, साहित्यकार), not 'to act too soon' (that is the meaning of 'jump the gun'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'burn one's fingers'
opts: to find fault with a gift
to do the same as someone else
exp: 'burn one's fingers' means 'to suffer loss through meddling' (Hindi: हाथ जलाना, नुक़सान उठाना). The other options are the meanings of 'look a gift horse in the mouth'; 'cat and dog life'; 'follow suit' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a memorable or important day'
exp: 'a red letter day' means 'a memorable or important day' (Hindi: यादगार/महत्वपूर्ण दिन). Others: 'foot the bill' = to pay the bill; 'see red' = to become very angry; 'take French leave' = to leave without permission.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'impossible'
exp: 'out of the question' means 'impossible' (Hindi: असंभव). Others: 'put two and two together' = to draw a conclusion from facts; 'cut both ways' = to have both good and bad effects; 'call it a day' = to stop working for the day.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make something clearly understood'
exp: 'drive home' means 'to make something clearly understood' (Hindi: अच्छी तरह समझाना). Others: 'take into account' = to consider; 'on the house' = free, paid for by the owner; 'a song and dance' = a fuss.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'completely extinct or out of date'
opts: Make hay while the sun shines
exp: 'as dead as a dodo' means 'completely extinct or out of date' (Hindi: पूरी तरह लुप्त). Others: 'die in harness' = to die while still working; 'rest on one's laurels' = to be satisfied with past success and stop trying; 'make hay while the sun shines' = to make the best use of an opportunity.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to pay an excessive price'
exp: 'pay through the nose' means 'to pay an excessive price' (Hindi: बहुत अधिक क़ीमत चुकाना). Others: 'bread and butter' = means of living; 'a wolf at the door' = threat of starvation or poverty; 'in the teeth of' = in spite of strong opposition.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to suffer loss through meddling'
exp: 'burn one's fingers' means 'to suffer loss through meddling' (Hindi: हाथ जलाना, नुक़सान उठाना). Others: 'cold comfort' = little or no consolation; 'at random' = without any plan or purpose; 'lay one's hands on' = to obtain or get hold of.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'see the light'
opts: to become nervous and lose courage
exp: 'see the light' means 'to understand something at last' (Hindi: समझ आ जाना). The other options are the meanings of 'safe and sound'; 'down to earth'; 'get cold feet' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'throw cold water on'
opts: to be ruined; to fail in business
exp: 'throw cold water on' means 'to discourage' (Hindi: हतोत्साहित करना, पानी फेरना). The other options are the meanings of 'go to the wall'; 'a song and dance'; 'stand one's ground' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to sell very quickly'
exp: 'sell like hot cakes' means 'to sell very quickly' (Hindi: हाथों-हाथ बिकना). Others: 'by fits and starts' = irregularly; not continuously; 'a queer fish' = a strange person; 'a snake in the grass' = a hidden enemy.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'show the white feather'
opts: to waste effort on a finished matter
to have a false sense of happiness
exp: 'show the white feather' means 'to show cowardice' (Hindi: कायरता दिखाना). The other options are the meanings of 'live in a fool's paradise'; 'flog a dead horse'; 'by leaps and bounds' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a cold war'
opts: a state of hostility without actual fighting
a person or thing everyone is talking about
exp: 'a cold war' means 'a state of hostility without actual fighting' (Hindi: शीत युद्ध, अप्रत्यक्ष शत्रुता). The other options are the meanings of 'the talk of the town'; 'come to terms with'; 'call off' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to pass to another owner'
exp: 'change hands' means 'to pass to another owner' (Hindi: स्वामित्व बदलना). Others: 'eat one's words' = to take back what one has said; 'a dead heat' = a race or contest in which two finish exactly level; 'an open secret' = something supposed to be secret but known to all.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a nine days' wonder'
opts: something that attracts attention for a short time
a friend who deserts you in times of trouble
exp: 'a nine days' wonder' means 'something that attracts attention for a short time' (Hindi: क्षणिक आकर्षण की वस्तु). The other options are the meanings of 'a fair-weather friend'; 'bad blood'; 'put one's foot down' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to reveal'
exp: 'bring to light' means 'to reveal' (Hindi: प्रकाश में लाना). Others: 'get wind of' = to hear about something secretly; 'carry the day' = to win; 'come to terms with' = to accept a difficult situation.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'by hook or by crook'
opts: by any means, fair or foul
to regret something that cannot be undone
exp: 'by hook or by crook' means 'by any means, fair or foul' (Hindi: किसी भी तरह, येन-केन-प्रकारेण). The other options are the meanings of 'cry over spilt milk'; 'crocodile tears'; 'a thorn in the flesh' respectively.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Ride roughshod over; (B) An ugly duckling; (C) Cry over spilt milk; (D) By hook or by crook
List-II: (1) to treat harshly without consideration; (2) by any means, fair or foul; (3) to regret something that cannot be undone; (4) a plain child who grows into a beautiful adult
exp: Correct matching: 'ride roughshod over' = to treat harshly without consideration; 'an ugly duckling' = a plain child who grows into a beautiful adult; 'cry over spilt milk' = to regret something that cannot be undone; 'by hook or by crook' = by any means, fair or foul. Hence A-1, B-4, C-3, D-2.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'grease the palm'
opts: a person unsuited to his job
exp: 'grease the palm' means 'to bribe' (Hindi: रिश्वत देना). The other options are the meanings of 'a thorn in the flesh'; 'ride roughshod over'; 'square peg in a round hole' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'give in'
opts: something supposed to be secret but known to all
exp: 'give in' means 'to surrender; to stop resisting' (Hindi: हार मानना). The other options are the meanings of 'see red'; 'be all and end all'; 'an open secret' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a large payment given to someone leaving a job'
exp: 'a golden handshake' means 'a large payment given to someone leaving a job' (Hindi: सेवानिवृत्ति पर दी जाने वाली बड़ी राशि). Others: 'a moot point' = a debatable question; 'an armchair critic' = one who criticises without practical experience; 'mince matters' = to speak evasively to avoid offending.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'go to the wall'
opts: to face all kinds of risks and dangers
to be ruined; to fail in business
exp: 'go to the wall' means 'to be ruined; to fail in business' (Hindi: बर्बाद हो जाना). The other options are the meanings of 'get into hot water'; 'go through fire and water'; 'put up with' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Blow hot and cold – very rarely
Once in a blue moon – to tease or make fun of someone
Pull one's leg – to keep changing one's opinion
Over head and ears – deeply, completely (in debt or love)
exp: 'over head and ears' means 'deeply, completely (in debt or love)' (पूरी तरह डूबा हुआ). Correct meanings of the others: 'once in a blue moon' = very rarely; 'pull one's leg' = to tease or make fun of someone; 'blow hot and cold' = to keep changing one's opinion.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'cast a slur'
opts: to stop something at an early stage
a task that has no hope of success
exp: 'cast a slur' means 'to bring disgrace to' (Hindi: कलंक लगाना). The other options are the meanings of 'an Achilles' heel'; 'nip in the bud'; 'a fool's errand' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'get wind of'
opts: to face all kinds of risks and dangers
exp: 'get wind of' means 'to hear about something secretly' (Hindi: भनक लगना). The other options are the meanings of 'walk of life'; 'give and take'; 'go through fire and water' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'at a loss'
opts: unable to decide what to do
exp: 'at a loss' means 'unable to decide what to do' (Hindi: किंकर्तव्यविमूढ़, असमंजस में). The other options are the meanings of 'in the long run'; 'put one's foot in it'; 'off and on' respectively.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) Burn one's fingers; (B) A piece of cake; (C) On the cards; (D) Root and branch
List-II: (1) thoroughly, completely; (2) something very easy to do; (3) likely to happen; (4) to suffer loss through meddling
exp: Correct matching: 'burn one's fingers' = to suffer loss through meddling; 'a piece of cake' = something very easy to do; 'on the cards' = likely to happen; 'root and branch' = thoroughly, completely. Hence A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'an idea that is unlikely to be true'
exp: 'a far-fetched idea' means 'an idea that is unlikely to be true' (Hindi: असंभाव्य विचार). Others: 'rest on one's laurels' = to be satisfied with past success and stop trying; 'a hornet's nest' = a situation full of trouble and anger; 'call a spade a spade' = to speak plainly and frankly.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'alpha and omega'
opts: to be in a risky situation
to support in words but not in deeds
exp: 'alpha and omega' means 'the beginning and the end' (Hindi: आदि और अंत). The other options are the meanings of 'pay lip service'; 'take to one's heels'; 'skate on thin ice' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'in the long run'
opts: to stop working for the day
exp: 'in the long run' means 'eventually' (Hindi: अंततः, लंबे समय में). The other options are the meanings of 'call it a day'; 'give and take'; 'man in the street' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'between two equally dangerous alternatives'
opts: Between the devil and the deep sea
exp: 'between the devil and the deep sea' means 'between two equally dangerous alternatives' (Hindi: दो विपत्तियों के बीच). Others: 'fly in the face of' = to openly defy; 'a rolling stone' = a person who does not settle in one place or job; 'hit below the belt' = to act unfairly.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Cross swords – to fight or argue
Pour oil on troubled waters – cowardly
Within an ace of – to calm a quarrel
exp: 'cross swords' means 'to fight or argue' (झगड़ना, बहस करना). Correct meanings of the others: 'pour oil on troubled waters' = to calm a quarrel; 'chicken-hearted' = cowardly; 'within an ace of' = very close to.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'an inexperienced person'
exp: 'a green horn' means 'an inexperienced person' (Hindi: अनाड़ी, नौसिखिया). Others: 'make one's blood boil' = to make someone very angry; 'skate on thin ice' = to be in a risky situation; 'look before you leap' = think carefully before acting.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: A sop to Cerberus – a bribe to quieten a troublesome person
A dog's life – a miserable existence
Die in harness – to die while still working
Make amends – to waste effort on a finished matter
exp: 'make amends' means 'to compensate for a wrong' (भरपाई करना), not 'to waste effort on a finished matter' (that is the meaning of 'flog a dead horse'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to surrender; to stop resisting'
exp: 'give in' means 'to surrender; to stop resisting' (Hindi: हार मानना). Others: 'at large' = free and not captured; 'be all and end all' = the most important part; 'a fish out of water' = a person in an unfamiliar and uncomfortable situation.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'rise like a phoenix'
exp: 'rise like a phoenix' means 'to rise again after destruction' (Hindi: राख से पुनः उठ खड़ा होना). The other options are the meanings of 'draw a blank'; 'ups and downs'; 'alpha and omega' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
opts: Hold one's tongue – to make a bad situation worse
Blow hot and cold – to keep changing one's opinion
A tall order – a very difficult demand
A drop in the ocean – a very small amount compared with what is needed
exp: 'hold one's tongue' means 'to keep quiet' (चुप रहना), not 'to make a bad situation worse' (that is the meaning of 'add fuel to the fire'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'cut to the quick'

exp: 'cut to the quick' means 'to hurt deeply' (Hindi: गहरी चोट पहुँचाना). The other options are the meanings of 'on the house'; 'get into hot water'; 'catch one's eye' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'run in the family'
opts: to be a common trait in a family
exp: 'run in the family' means 'to be a common trait in a family' (Hindi: ख़ानदानी गुण होना). The other options are the meanings of 'get into hot water'; 'after one's own heart'; 'wind up' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Jump the gun – to act too soon
Get the upper hand – ordinary members of an organisation
A household name – to gain an advantage
Rank and file – a person or thing that is very well known
exp: 'jump the gun' means 'to act too soon' (जल्दबाज़ी में काम करना). Correct meanings of the others: 'a household name' = a person or thing that is very well known; 'get the upper hand' = to gain an advantage; 'rank and file' = ordinary members of an organisation.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'at a premium'
exp: 'at a premium' means 'in great demand; scarce' (Hindi: बहुत माँग में). The other options are the meanings of 'rank and file'; 'all ears'; 'a piece of cake' respectively.

opts: in every way; thoroughly (as in "every inch a gentleman")
a little-known person who unexpectedly wins or succeeds
exp: 'kick up a row' means 'to create a disturbance' (Hindi: हंगामा खड़ा करना). The other options are the meanings of 'every inch'; 'once in a blue moon'; 'a dark horse' respectively.

q: Which of the following idioms is CORRECTLY matched with its meaning?
opts: Every inch – a decisive test of value or quality
Look a gift horse in the mouth – to find fault with a gift
Fly off the handle – in every way; thoroughly (as in "every inch a gentleman")
An acid test – to lose one's temper suddenly

q: Which of the following idioms is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
