Rain cats and dogs – to rain very heavily
Wash one's hands of – to try every possible means to achieve something
An arm and a leg – a very high price
exp: 'wash one's hands of' means 'to refuse to have anything more to do with' (पल्ला झाड़ लेना), not 'to try every possible means to achieve something' (that is the meaning of 'move heaven and earth'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a blessing in disguise'

something good that at first seemed bad
the ability to speak fluently and persuasively
exp: 'a blessing in disguise' means 'something good that at first seemed bad' (Hindi: छिपा हुआ वरदान). The other options are the meanings of 'at daggers drawn'; 'a gift of the gab'; 'nip in the bud' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a practical method based on experience'
exp: 'a rule of thumb' means 'a practical method based on experience' (Hindi: अनुभव पर आधारित नियम). Others: 'pull strings' = to use one's influence secretly; 'throw in the towel' = to admit defeat; 'in high spirits' = very cheerful.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'miss the boat'
exp: 'miss the boat' means 'to lose an opportunity' (Hindi: अवसर गँवाना). The other options are the meanings of 'not one's cup of tea'; 'rain cats and dogs'; 'go Dutch' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to avoid starvation'
opts: Keep the wolf from the door
Let the grass grow under one's feet
exp: 'keep the wolf from the door' means 'to avoid starvation' (Hindi: भुखमरी से बचना). Others: 'cat and dog life' = a life full of quarrels; 'a household name' = a person or thing that is very well known; 'let the grass grow under one's feet' = to delay or waste time.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'fall flat'
opts: to gain an advantage over someone by acting first
to fail to produce the intended effect
to try every possible means to achieve something
exp: 'fall flat' means 'to fail to produce the intended effect' (Hindi: असफल होना, प्रभावहीन रहना). The other options are the meanings of 'steal a march on'; 'blow hot and cold'; 'move heaven and earth' respectively.

q:
Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:
List-I: (A) A sitting duck; (B) Sell like hot cakes; (C) Have a finger in every pie; (D) Set the Thames on fire
List-II: (1) to sell very quickly; (2) an easy target; (3) to do something remarkable; (4) to be involved in many activities
exp: Correct matching: 'a sitting duck' = an easy target; 'sell like hot cakes' = to sell very quickly; 'have a finger in every pie' = to be involved in many activities; 'set the Thames on fire' = to do something remarkable. Hence A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'a cock and bull story'
opts: a hope or plan that is very unlikely to be realised
to be contrary to one's nature
exp: 'a cock and bull story' means 'an absurd, unbelievable story' (Hindi: मनगढ़ंत कहानी). The other options are the meanings of 'throw in the towel'; 'go against the grain'; 'a pie in the sky' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'hue and cry'
opts: to make impractical plans; to daydream
completely puzzled and not knowing what to do
exp: 'hue and cry' means 'a loud public protest' (Hindi: शोर-शराबा, हो-हल्ला). The other options are the meanings of 'at one's wit's end'; 'build castles in the air'; 'at daggers drawn' respectively.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'turn a deaf ear'
opts: to remain neutral; to be undecided
exp: 'turn a deaf ear' means 'to refuse to listen' (Hindi: अनसुना करना). The other options are the meanings of 'keep up appearances'; 'as the crow flies'; 'sit on the fence' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to stop working for the day'
exp: 'call it a day' means 'to stop working for the day' (Hindi: दिन का काम समाप्त करना). Others: 'play with fire' = to do something dangerous; 'a fish out of water' = a person in an unfamiliar and uncomfortable situation; 'a shot in the dark' = a wild guess.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to create a disturbance'
exp: 'kick up a row' means 'to create a disturbance' (Hindi: हंगामा खड़ा करना). Others: 'in the same boat' = in the same difficult situation; 'a wolf at the door' = threat of starvation or poverty; 'a square meal' = a full and satisfying meal.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a person who changes sides or principles'
exp: 'a turncoat' means 'a person who changes sides or principles' (Hindi: दलबदलू). Others: 'at arm's length' = at a distance, avoiding close contact; 'by leaps and bounds' = very rapidly; 'lion's share' = the largest part.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to be impossible to describe'
exp: 'beggar description' means 'to be impossible to describe' (Hindi: वर्णन से परे होना). Others: 'off the cuff' = without preparation; 'a fly in the ointment' = a small flaw that spoils something; 'a pretty kettle of fish' = an awkward or difficult situation.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'vote with one's feet'
opts: to have both good and bad effects
exp: 'vote with one's feet' means 'to show disapproval by leaving' (Hindi: विरोध में छोड़ जाना). The other options are the meanings of 'look down upon'; 'cut both ways'; 'call off' respectively.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'one who criticises without practical experience'
exp: 'an armchair critic' means 'one who criticises without practical experience' (Hindi: बिना अनुभव का आलोचक). Others: 'weal and woe' = prosperity and adversity; 'walk on eggshells' = to be very careful not to upset someone; 'an ugly duckling' = a plain child who grows into a beautiful adult.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'something good that at first seemed bad'
exp: 'a blessing in disguise' means 'something good that at first seemed bad' (Hindi: छिपा हुआ वरदान). Others: 'a far-fetched idea' = an idea that is unlikely to be true; 'hue and cry' = a loud public protest; 'yeoman's service' = very useful service or help.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'a selfish motive'
exp: 'an axe to grind' means 'a selfish motive' (Hindi: निजी स्वार्थ). Others: 'null and void' = invalid; having no legal force; 'rub salt into the wound' = to make a painful situation worse; 'take to one's heels' = to run away.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to keep at a distance'
exp: 'keep at bay' means 'to keep at a distance' (Hindi: दूर रखना). Others: 'in a tight corner' = in a difficult situation with little room to escape; 'blow hot and cold' = to keep changing one's opinion; 'move heaven and earth' = to try every possible means to achieve something.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to be defeated or killed'
exp: 'bite the dust' means 'to be defeated or killed' (Hindi: पराजित होना, धूल चाटना). Others: 'bell the cat' = to undertake a dangerous task; 'draw the line' = to set a limit; 'keep one's fingers crossed' = to hope for the best.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'at one's beck and call'

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to go to bed'
exp: 'hit the sack' means 'to go to bed' (Hindi: सोने जाना). Others: 'within an ace of' = very close to; 'a green horn' = an inexperienced person; 'a sitting duck' = an easy target.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to make unnecessarily fine distinctions'

Make a clean breast of – to confess fully
exp: 'end in smoke' means 'to come to nothing' (निष्फल होना), not 'under suspicion' (that is the meaning of 'under a cloud'). The other pairs are correct.

q: Choose the idiom/phrase that means: 'to reflect or think deeply'
exp: 'chew the cud' means 'to reflect or think deeply' (Hindi: गहराई से विचार करना). Others: 'a storm in a teacup' = a lot of fuss about a small matter; 'a damp squib' = something that turns out to be disappointing; 'blow one's own trumpet' = to praise oneself.

Match the idioms in List-I with their meanings in List-II:

exp: Correct matching: 'a damp squib' = something that turns out to be disappointing; 'as cool as a cucumber' = very calm and composed; 'as fit as a fiddle' = in very good health; 'a moot point' = a debatable question. Hence A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4.

to change one's behaviour for the better

exp: 'a lame excuse' means 'an unconvincing excuse' (Hindi: लचर बहाना). Others: 'turn the tables' = to reverse a situation to one's advantage; 'a green horn' = an inexperienced person; 'feel the pinch' = to experience financial hardship.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'come to a head'
exp: 'come to a head' means 'to reach a crisis' (Hindi: चरम सीमा पर पहुँचना). The other options are the meanings of 'with a high hand'; 'see red'; 'cut a sorry figure' respectively.

q:

List-I: (A) Hue and cry; (B) In a jiffy; (C) Mind one's p's and q's; (D) Cast pearls before swine
List-II: (1) very quickly; (2) a loud public protest; (3) to offer something valuable to those who cannot appreciate it; (4) to be careful about one's behaviour
exp: Correct matching: 'hue and cry' = a loud public protest; 'in a jiffy' = very quickly; 'mind one's p's and q's' = to be careful about one's behaviour; 'cast pearls before swine' = to offer something valuable to those who cannot appreciate it. Hence A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom/phrase: 'at a stone's throw'

q:

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is remembered as the 'Iron Man of India'. After independence in 1947, the country faced a difficult task: more than five hundred princely states had to be joined with the Indian Union. Some rulers were willing to join, while others hesitated or wished to remain independent. Patel, who was the first Home Minister, handled the situation with patience as well as firmness. He persuaded most rulers through discussion, assuring them of respect and certain privileges. Where persuasion failed, he did not hesitate to take strong action. Within a short period, almost all the states had become part of India. Historians agree that without his practical wisdom and determination, the map of India might have looked very different. His birthday, 31 October, is now observed as National Unity Day.

Question: Which post did Patel hold after independence, according to the passage?
exp: Answer: 'The first Home Minister'. The passage says Patel was the first Home Minister.

The invention of the printing press in the fifteenth century changed the world in ways its inventor could hardly have imagined. Before printing, books were copied by hand, a slow and costly process that kept them in the hands of a few rich people and religious institutions. Once books could be produced quickly and cheaply, ideas began to travel faster than ever before. Scientists could share their discoveries, reformers could spread their arguments, and ordinary people could learn to read. Some rulers feared this new freedom and tried to control what was printed, but they could not stop the flow of knowledge entirely. Many historians therefore compare the printing press to the internet of our own time: both made information widely available and, in doing so, challenged the authority of those who had once controlled it.

Question: Before the printing press, how were books produced?
exp: Answer: 'They were copied by hand'. Before printing, books were copied by hand.

A common mistake in discussions about poverty is to treat the poor as passive recipients of help rather than as active agents with their own plans and abilities. Programmes designed without consulting the people they are meant to serve often fail; a well built but poorly located hospital may stand empty, and a free cooking stove may be used as a storage shelf if it does not suit local cooking habits. By contrast, schemes that involve communities in planning and decision-making tend to be more effective, because local people understand their needs and constraints. Self-help groups of rural women, for example, have shown that with access to small loans and training, poor families can build businesses, educate their children and gain confidence. Dignity, not merely charity, lies at the heart of lasting development.

A single lamp does not banish all the darkness of the night; it simply makes a small space visible and safe. Similarly, no individual can remove all the ignorance or suffering in the world. What each person can do is illuminate the small circle around him through kindness, honesty and learning. When many such lamps are lit, the darkness retreats. In serious cases such as heavy bleeding, fractures or unconsciousness, first aid is only a temporary measure until professional help arrives. q:
Read the following passage and answer the question.

Corruption is frequently discussed as though it were a problem only of greedy officials. In reality, it is sustained by a wider web of participants. The citizen who pays a bribe to skip a queue, the businessman who offers a 'gift' to win a contract and the bystander who shrugs and says that nothing can change all help to keep the system alive. Laws and vigilance agencies are indispensable, but they cannot succeed if society quietly tolerates small acts of dishonesty. Technology has helped in some areas: online applications and direct transfers of benefits have reduced opportunities for middlemen. Yet the most durable safeguard is a culture in which dishonesty is regarded as shameful rather than clever. Such a culture is built in homes and schools long before it is tested in offices.

Question: Consider the statements: I. Laws alone are sufficient to end corruption. II. Values learnt at home and school help fight corruption. Which is/are correct according to the passage?
exp: Answer: 'Only II'. Laws are indispensable but not enough (I is wrong); a culture built in homes and schools matters (II is correct).

Reading habits have changed greatly in the last two decades. Earlier, a student who wanted information on a topic had to visit a library, search through catalogues and spend hours turning pages. Today the same information appears on a mobile screen within seconds. This speed is certainly useful, but it has a hidden cost. Many teachers notice that students now skim rather than read; they jump from one link to another and rarely finish a long article. Deep reading, in which the mind slowly follows an argument and questions it, needs patience and silence. Psychologists believe that this kind of reading strengthens memory, imagination and the ability to concentrate. Therefore, while we enjoy the convenience of digital information, we should also set aside some time every day for reading a book quietly, without notifications and without hurry.

Question: In the past, where did a student usually go to find information on a topic?
exp: Answer: 'A library'. Earlier, a student had to visit a library to get information on a topic.

Employers increasingly value such experience when they select candidates. Moreover, volunteers build friendships with people from different backgrounds, which widens their understanding of society. Of course, the main purpose of volunteering should remain the service of others. But it is encouraging to know that kindness, like a good investment, returns more than it costs.

The humble bicycle is enjoying a revival in many cities. Once considered the vehicle of the poor, it is now chosen by students, office workers and fitness enthusiasts alike. The reasons are easy to see. Cycling costs almost nothing, produces no pollution and provides excellent exercise. In crowded city centres, a bicycle can often reach a destination faster than a car stuck in traffic. Yet cyclists in Indian cities face real dangers, because roads are designed mainly for motor vehicles and drivers rarely give way to them. Cities that have built separate cycle lanes and public bicycle-sharing systems have seen the number of cyclists rise sharply. The experience suggests that people will cycle in large numbers if they feel safe doing so.

In a country like India, where many languages are spoken, knowing more than one language is also a practical necessity for work and travel. Some parents worry that learning two languages at once may confuse young children. Studies, however, indicate that children are remarkably capable of learning several languages, and any early mixing of words usually disappears as they grow. The earlier a child is exposed to a language, the more naturally it is acquired.

The camel is perfectly suited to life in the desert. Its hump stores fat, not water as many believe, and this fat can be broken down for energy when food is scarce. A camel can drink over a hundred litres of water in a few minutes and then go for days without drinking again. Its thick eyelashes and the ability to close its nostrils protect it from blowing sand. Wide, padded feet prevent it from sinking into soft sand, and its body temperature can rise during the day without harm, reducing the need to sweat and lose water. Because of these qualities, the camel has been called the 'ship of the desert'. For centuries it carried goods and people across vast dry regions where no other animal could survive.

It reduces the need to sweat and lose water

As a result, most girls left school after the fifth class. Then a retired teacher named Ramdayal decided to change things. He began teaching a few children on the verandah of his house, free of cost. Slowly the number of students grew, and the villagers, impressed by his dedication, contributed bricks, cement and labour to build two classrooms. Within three years the government recognised the school and appointed regular teachers. Today, every girl in Sukhpur completes at least the eighth class. When asked about his achievement, Ramdayal simply says that he lit a small lamp and the village supplied the oil.

Every household produces waste, but how we handle it makes a world of difference. When wet kitchen waste is mixed with plastic, glass and paper, it becomes difficult to recycle anything, and most of it ends up in overflowing landfills. Segregating waste at the source, that is, in our homes, solves much of this problem. Wet waste such as vegetable peels can be turned into compost that enriches the soil. Dry waste such as paper, metal and certain plastics can be sold to recyclers. Hazardous items like batteries and medicines need separate disposal. Several Indian cities, including Indore, have shown that when citizens cooperate with municipal bodies, streets become cleaner and landfills shrink. The lesson is that cleanliness is not merely the duty of sweepers; it is a shared civic responsibility.

As an example of a city where citizen cooperation led to cleaner streets
As a city without municipal bodies
As a city that bans recycling

The tree also supports a great variety of living things. Birds feed on its small red figs, bats roost in its branches and insects find shelter in its bark. Long before the invention of the clock, people measured time by watching nature. The rising and setting of the sun marked the day, while the changing shape of the moon helped them count months. Farmers noticed that certain stars appeared in the night sky just before the rains, and they planned their sowing accordingly. Later, sundials used the moving shadow of a stick to show the hour, and water clocks measured time by the steady flow of water from one vessel to another. These devices were not very accurate, but they were sufficient for a world in which most work followed the rhythm of daylight. Only with the growth of factories and railways did people need to know the exact minute, and clocks became a part of everyday life.

Similar stories exist about the discovery of X-rays and the microwave oven. In each case, the scientist had the knowledge to recognise that something unusual was important. As the French scientist Louis Pasteur famously remarked, chance favours only the prepared mind. Accidents may open the door, but it takes a trained and curious person to walk through it.

Modern gossip, however, can spread far beyond the community in which it began, especially through social media, and it is often based on rumour rather than fact. A careless remark can now damage a reputation across a city within hours. The ancient function of gossip thus survives, but its scale and speed have turned a useful social tool into a potentially dangerous weapon.

Many of us carry a mental picture of the 'ideal' life: a well-paid job, a large house, a fancy car. We assume that once we reach these goals, happiness will follow automatically. Psychologists call this the arrival fallacy. Surveys repeatedly show that after the initial excitement of a promotion or a new purchase fades, people return to roughly the same level of satisfaction as before. This does not mean that ambition is pointless. It means that lasting contentment comes less from reaching destinations than from the quality of the journey: meaningful work, close relationships, good health and a sense of contributing to something larger than oneself. Those who learn to find joy in the process rather than postponing it to some imagined future are, on the whole, happier.

However, rising sea levels and the (4)______ of mangroves for farming and fish ponds threaten this unique ecosystem. Scientists warn that losing the mangroves would leave millions of people (5)______ to disasters. Protecting them is therefore not a luxury but a (6)______. Local communities, who depend on the forest for honey and fish, must be made (7)______ in conservation, for no plan imposed from outside can succeed (8)______ their support.
exp: Blank (7): 'partners'. 'made partners in conservation' — a plural noun is needed.

q:
In the following passage (Cloze Test), choose the most appropriate option for blank (1).

Every morning my grandfather goes (1)______ a walk in the park near our house. He says that walking is the (2)______ exercise because it costs nothing and can be done at any age. He has been following this habit (3)______ more than forty years. On his way back, he (4)______ fresh vegetables from the market and talks to the shopkeepers, (5)______ know him well. At home he reads the newspaper (6)______ breakfast and then waters the plants in our small garden. Although he is now seventy-five, he is (7)______ active than many young people I know. Whenever I feel lazy, I think of him and feel (8)______ to get up and move.
exp: Blank (1): 'for'. 'go for a walk' is the correct collocation.

q:
In the following passage (Cloze Test), choose the most appropriate option for blank (7).

Kabir was a poet and saint who lived in the fifteenth century. He was brought up (1)______ a family of weavers in Varanasi. Although he had little formal education, his couplets, known as dohas, are full (2)______ deep wisdom. He criticised blind faith and empty rituals and (3)______ people to love God with a pure heart. His language was simple, so even the common people could (4)______ his message easily. Many of his dohas are still (5)______ in schools today. One famous doha advises us not to (6)______ for tomorrow what can be done today. Kabir believed that all human beings are (7)______, whatever their religion or caste. That is why he is respected by people of all (8)______.
exp: Blank (7): 'equal'. Kabir believed that all human beings are equal.

q:
In the following passage (Cloze Test), choose the most appropriate option for blank (6).

Ambition is a powerful force that drives people to (1)______ their potential. Without it, many great inventions, discoveries and works of art would never have been created. Yet ambition, like fire, must be (2)______. When it becomes excessive, it can lead people to (3)______ their health, their families and even their principles in pursuit of success. History is full of rulers whose (4)______ ambition brought ruin upon themselves and their nations. Healthy ambition, on the other hand, is (5)______ by values; it seeks achievement without trampling on others. It also (6)______ room for contentment, recognising that success is a means to a good life rather than an end in itself. The wise, therefore, cultivate ambition but keep it on a (7)______, ensuring that it remains a servant of their (8)______ and not their master.
exp: Blank (6): 'leaves'. Subject 'It' is singular — 'It also leaves room for contentment'.

q:
कथन: "अपने बच्चों को पोलियो की खुराक अवश्य पिलाएँ।" — स्वास्थ्य विभाग का विज्ञापन
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. लोग विज्ञापन पढ़ते/देखते हैं।
II. पोलियो की खुराक बच्चों के लिए लाभदायक है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Do get your children the polio dose." — Health department advertisement
Assumptions:
I. People read/see advertisements.
II. The polio dose is beneficial for children.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
विज्ञापन इसी विश्वास पर दिया जाता है कि लोग उसे देखेंगे (I) और विभाग खुराक को लाभदायक मानता है, तभी पिलाने को कह रहा है (II)। दोनों निहित हैं।
अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: "कृपया पानी व्यर्थ न बहाएँ।" — नगर निगम की सूचना
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. लोग सूचना का पालन करेंगे।
II. नगर में पानी की बिल्कुल कमी नहीं है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Please do not waste water." — Municipal corporation notice
Assumptions:
I. People will follow the notice.
II. There is no shortage of water at all in the city.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
सूचना इस विश्वास से दी जाती है कि लोग पालन करेंगे (I निहित)। II तो सूचना की भावना के विपरीत है, अतः निहित नहीं।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: परीक्षा में अच्छे अंक पाने के लिए नियमित अध्ययन कीजिए। — शिक्षक की सलाह
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. नियमित अध्ययन से अंक सुधर सकते हैं।
II. विद्यार्थी अच्छे अंक पाना चाहते हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: Study regularly to score good marks in the examination. — Teacher's advice
Assumptions:
I. Regular study can improve marks.
II. Students want to score good marks.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
सलाह तभी दी जाती है जब शिक्षक मानता है कि नियमित अध्ययन से लाभ होगा (I) और विद्यार्थी अच्छे अंक चाहते हैं (II)। दोनों निहित।
अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: "यातायात नियमों का पालन करें, दुर्घटना से बचें।" — यातायात पुलिस
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. नियमों के पालन से दुर्घटनाएँ कम होती हैं।
II. सभी दुर्घटनाएँ केवल नियम तोड़ने से ही होती हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Follow traffic rules, avoid accidents." — Traffic police
Assumptions:
I. Following rules reduces accidents.
II. All accidents happen only due to breaking rules.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
I निहित है, तभी अपील की गई। II 'सभी' और 'केवल' वाला अतिवादी कथन है, निहित नहीं।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: राम ने श्याम से कहा, "कल सुबह 6 बजे मुझे स्टेशन पर मिलना।"
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. श्याम के पास घड़ी नहीं है।
II. स्टेशन पर हमेशा भीड़ रहती है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: Ram told Shyam, "Meet me at the station at 6 tomorrow morning."
Assumptions:
I. Shyam does not have a watch.
II. The station is always crowded.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
कथन में न घड़ी का कोई संकेत है न भीड़ का; दोनों में से कोई भी पूर्वधारणा निहित नहीं है।
अतः सही उत्तर: न तो I और न ही II निहित है।

q:
कथन: विद्यालय की सूचना: "कल से विद्यालय सुबह 8 बजे के स्थान पर 7 बजे लगेगा।"
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. विद्यार्थी और शिक्षक सूचना को पढ़कर समय पर आएँगे।
II. 7 बजे विद्यालय आना सभी के लिए असंभव है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: School notice: "From tomorrow school will start at 7 a.m. instead of 8 a.m."
Assumptions:
I. Students and teachers will read the notice and come on time.
II. It is impossible for everyone to come at 7.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
सूचना जारी करने वाला मानता है कि सूचना पढ़ी जाएगी और पालन होगा (I)। II सूचना के उद्देश्य के विपरीत है।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: "हमारा साबुन खरीदें, त्वचा को कोमल बनाएँ।" — एक विज्ञापन
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. अन्य सभी साबुन त्वचा को कठोर बनाते हैं।
II. लोग कोमल त्वचा चाहते हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Buy our soap and make your skin soft." — An advertisement
Assumptions:
I. All other soaps make the skin hard.
II. People want soft skin.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
विज्ञापन लोगों की कोमल त्वचा की चाह पर आधारित है (II निहित)। अन्य साबुनों के बारे में कोई तुलना नहीं की गई, अतः I निहित नहीं।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:
कथन: मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा, "राज्य के हर गाँव तक पक्की सड़क पहुँचाई जाएगी।"
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. अभी कुछ गाँवों तक पक्की सड़क नहीं है।
II. सरकार इस कार्य के लिए संसाधन जुटा सकती है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: The Chief Minister said, "A paved road will be taken to every village of the state."
Assumptions:
I. At present some villages do not have paved roads.
II. The government can arrange resources for this work.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
घोषणा तभी सार्थक है जब कुछ गाँवों में सड़क न हो (I) और सरकार मानती हो कि वह यह कर सकती है (II)। दोनों निहित।
अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: "कार्यालय में मोबाइल फोन बंद रखें।" — कार्यालय प्रमुख का निर्देश
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. मोबाइल फोन से कार्य में बाधा आती है।
II. कर्मचारी मोबाइल फोन का उपयोग करना नहीं जानते।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Keep mobile phones switched off in the office." — Head of office's instruction
Assumptions:
I. Mobile phones disturb work.
II. Employees do not know how to use mobile phones.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
निर्देश के पीछे यही धारणा है कि फोन से कार्य बाधित होता है (I)। II निराधार है।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: "सावधान! आगे तीव्र मोड़ है।" — सड़क किनारे लगा बोर्ड
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. सभी चालक लापरवाह होते हैं।
II. बोर्ड देखकर चालक सावधान हो जाएँगे।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Caution! Sharp turn ahead." — A roadside board
Assumptions:
I. All drivers are careless.
II. Drivers will become cautious on seeing the board.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
बोर्ड इसी विश्वास पर लगाया जाता है कि चालक उसे देखकर सावधानी बरतेंगे (II)। 'सभी चालक लापरवाह' अतिवादी है (I नहीं)।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:
कथन: सीता ने अपनी सहेली को जन्मदिन पर एक पुस्तक भेंट की।
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. सहेली के पास कोई पुस्तक नहीं थी।
II. पुस्तक बहुत महँगी थी।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: Sita gifted a book to her friend on her birthday.
Assumptions:
I. The friend had no books.
II. The book was very expensive.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
पुस्तक भेंट करने से न यह माना जा सकता कि सहेली के पास कोई पुस्तक नहीं थी, न यह कि पुस्तक महँगी थी। कोई निहित नहीं।
अतः सही उत्तर: न तो I और न ही II निहित है।

q:
कथन: "यदि आप इस बार वोट डालेंगे, तो अच्छी सरकार चुन सकेंगे।" — निर्वाचन आयोग की अपील
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. मतदान से अच्छी सरकार चुनने में सहायता मिलती है।
II. पिछली सभी सरकारें खराब थीं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "If you vote this time, you can elect a good government." — Election Commission appeal
Assumptions:
I. Voting helps in electing a good government.
II. All previous governments were bad.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
अपील I पर आधारित है। II के बारे में कथन में कुछ नहीं कहा गया।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: पिता ने पुत्र से कहा, "तुम इंजीनियरिंग की प्रवेश परीक्षा की तैयारी करो।"
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. पुत्र प्रवेश परीक्षा की तैयारी कर सकता है।
II. इंजीनियरिंग में प्रवेश परीक्षा के माध्यम से होता है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: The father told his son, "Prepare for the engineering entrance examination."
Assumptions:
I. The son is capable of preparing for the entrance exam.
II. Admission to engineering is through an entrance examination.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
सलाह तभी दी जाती है जब पुत्र को सक्षम माना जाए (I) और प्रवेश परीक्षा से होता हो (II)। दोनों निहित।
अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: "दिन में दो बार दाँत साफ़ करें।" — दंत चिकित्सक
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. दिन में तीन बार दाँत साफ़ करना हानिकारक है।
II. दिन में दो बार दाँत साफ़ करने से दाँत स्वस्थ रहते हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:
Statement: "Brush your teeth twice a day." — Dentist
Assumptions:
I. Brushing three times a day is harmful.
II. Brushing twice a day keeps teeth healthy.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit

अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:

q:
कथन: "मैं कल दिल्ली जाऊँगा।" — अमित
पूर्वधारणाएँ:

q:
कथन: "सुबह की सैर स्वास्थ्य के लिए लाभदायक है, रोज़ टहलें।" — एक डॉक्टर

II. लोग सलाह मानकर टहल सकते हैं।

qe:

Assumptions:

q:

पूर्वधारणाएँ:

II. सभी ग्राहक पिन भूल जाते हैं।

opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं

optse: Only assumption I is implicit

Both I and II are implicit

q:

पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. अधिकांश इच्छुक उम्मीदवार अंतिम तिथि तक आवेदन कर देंगे।
II. 30 जून के बाद वेबसाइट हमेशा के लिए बंद हो जाएगी।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:

Assumptions:

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है

अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:
कथन: सरकार ने सभी सरकारी कार्यालयों में बायोमेट्रिक उपस्थिति अनिवार्य कर दी है।
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. सभी कर्मचारी पहले कभी समय पर नहीं आते थे।
II. बायोमेट्रिक व्यवस्था से उपस्थिति में सुधार हो सकता है।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?

अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:
कथन: "इस वर्ष गेहूँ का समर्थन मूल्य बढ़ाया जाएगा ताकि किसानों की आय बढ़े।" — कृषि मंत्री
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. समर्थन मूल्य बढ़ने से किसानों की आय बढ़ सकती है।
II. किसान सरकार को समर्थन मूल्य पर गेहूँ बेचेंगे।

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं

अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: नगर निगम ने घोषणा की कि शहर में प्लास्टिक की थैलियों पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध रहेगा।
पूर्वधारणाएँ:

II. प्रतिबंध के बाद लोग खरीदारी करना बंद कर देंगे।

Only assumption II is implicit

अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:

पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. कर्मचारी पूरी तरह अयोग्य हैं।
II. प्रशिक्षण से कर्मचारियों की कार्यक्षमता बढ़ सकती है।

Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:
कथन: "अगले महीने से हमारी बस सेवा इंदौर से भोपाल के बीच हर घंटे चलेगी।" — एक बस कंपनी
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. इंदौर-भोपाल के बीच कोई अन्य बस नहीं चलती।
II. रेल सेवा इस मार्ग पर बंद हो जाएगी।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?

Assumptions:

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है

Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

अतः सही उत्तर: न तो I और न ही II निहित है।

q:
कथन: जिला कलेक्टर ने अधिकारियों को निर्देश दिया कि जनसुनवाई में आए हर आवेदन का निराकरण 15 दिनों में किया जाए।
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. अधिकांश आवेदनों का निराकरण 15 दिनों में संभव है।

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

निर्देश तभी दिया जाता है जब इसे व्यावहारिक माना जाए (I)। आवेदनों की संख्या कम होने की धारणा आवश्यक नहीं (II नहीं)।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:

पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. लोग डेंगू से बचना चाहते हैं।
II. लोग अपने आसपास जमा पानी हटा सकते हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?

Assumptions:

opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
अपील का आधार है कि लोग डेंगू से बचना चाहते हैं (I) और वे निर्देश पर अमल कर सकते हैं (II)। दोनों निहित।
अतः सही उत्तर: I और II दोनों निहित हैं।

q:
कथन: "हमने अपने रेस्तराँ में धूम्रपान निषेध क्षेत्र बनाया है।" — रेस्तराँ मालिक
पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. सभी ग्राहक धूम्रपान करते हैं।
II. कुछ ग्राहक धुएँ से मुक्त वातावरण पसंद करते हैं।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?

II. Some customers prefer a smoke-free environment.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit

निषेध क्षेत्र कुछ ग्राहकों की पसंद (II) को ध्यान में रखकर बनाया गया; 'सभी ग्राहक धूम्रपान करते हैं' निराधार है।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा II निहित है।

q:
कथन: "आवेदन-पत्र के साथ आधार कार्ड की स्व-प्रमाणित प्रति संलग्न करें।" — एक विभाग का निर्देश
पूर्वधारणाएँ:

II. आधार कार्ड के बिना कोई सरकारी कार्य नहीं हो सकता।
कथन में कौन-सी पूर्वधारणा/पूर्वधारणाएँ निहित है/हैं?
qe:

Assumptions:

II. No government work can be done without an Aadhaar card.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: I और II दोनों निहित हैं
न तो I और न ही II निहित है
optse: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
exp:
निर्देश तभी व्यावहारिक है जब आवेदकों के पास आधार हो (I)। II अतिवादी सामान्यीकरण है।
अतः सही उत्तर: केवल पूर्वधारणा I निहित है।

q:

पूर्वधारणाएँ:
I. लाल पेन से लिखा उत्तर पढ़ा नहीं जा सकता।
II. परीक्षार्थियों के पास केवल नीले पेन होते हैं।

qe:

II. Examinees have only blue pens.
